A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Federated ADMM from Bayesian Duality. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original regression and outlier experiments, federated neural-network results, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendices I–J.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and ablations in Section 4 and Appendices E and G, revises MNIST results, and reports an accuracy-versus-runtime comparison.

M1.justification: v2 Eqs. 12–14 and v3 Eqs. 15–17 specify the same updates under renamed variables. The full-covariance and diagonal-covariance variants are retained. Algorithm 1's explicit loss rescaling and Gaussian prior match the implementation already documented in v2 Appendix G.

E1.justification: Both versions use MNIST, FashionMNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and the same illustrative regression and outlier scenarios. The homogeneous and heterogeneous FashionMNIST blocks exchange positions between Tables 1 and 4; neither coverage is added nor removed. The runtime plot uses an existing MNIST setting.

E2.justification: The centralized batch-VON global-optimum reference described for v2's logistic-regression comparison in Appendix I.1 is omitted from v3's corresponding presentation and Appendix E.3. The named federated baselines and PVI/Bregman-ADMM comparator sets otherwise remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 Figure 2 adds accuracy evaluated against elapsed minutes for 100-client MNIST, supplementing evaluation by communication rounds. Existing splits, architectures, batch sizes, and stated training settings are retained. Adding 100 rounds to the summary prose documents checkpoints already present in v2 Table 2.

E4.justification: v3 Figure 2 adds a direct runtime-efficiency analysis comparing IVON-ADMM with FedAvg to examine computational overhead. The outlier study, IVON-PVI comparison, and temperature and client-step-size ablations are retained, including unchanged values in Tables 5–7.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over three runs or seeds. No additional runs, new uncertainty estimator, confidence intervals, or significance tests are documented. Changed MNIST standard deviations accompany revised results rather than a changed reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Two matched table rows change: the IVON-ADMM variants for highly heterogeneous MNIST in Table 2. For the ensemble, 100-round accuracy changes from 95.5±0.1 to 96.0±0.1 and NLL from 0.15±0.00 to 0.13±0.00 under the same stated setting. Figure 2 adds accuracy and timing trajectories; the previous NLL convergence panel is omitted, although checkpoint NLL values remain. Other matched table values are unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 adds explicit derivations of the dual-gradient identities in Appendices A and C.1 and corrects the full-Gaussian KL expansion from v2 Eq. 36 in v3 Eq. 47. The two propositions retain their substance after relocation. The new Appendix B.2 derivation introduces a prior-gradient sign inconsistency with its following equation.

C1.justification: The central claims remain Bayesian duality generalizing ADMM, recovery through isotropic Gaussians and the delta approximation, one-round convergence on quadratics, and an efficient IVON-ADMM variant with up to approximately seven percentage points of accuracy improvement. The fixed-point framing refines the explanation without materially changing these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 Section 3.5 and Appendix D.2 explicitly identify the matrix dual variable with the expected Hessian and explain its role in Newton-like updates. v2 supplies the underlying formulas but leaves this mechanistic connection largely implicit. Interpretations concerning uncertainty, outliers, and hyperparameter tradeoffs are retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds a first-page code-access link, absent from v2. Algorithm 1 also makes the scaled loss and server Gaussian prior explicit, clarifying information already supplied in v2 Appendix G. Most experimental hyperparameter, architecture, and data-processing disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 explicitly attributes the foundational VB fixed-point equations to Khan and Lin (2017) and Khan and Nielsen (2018), and adds information-geometry and expectation-propagation references. It trims the historical survey of distributed Bayesian methods and several ADMM references while retaining the central positioning relative to Swaroop et al., PVI, and Bregman ADMM.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and Sections 2–3 undergo extensive rewriting around a more explicit fixed-point and information-flow narrative. Terminology and notation change throughout, and Appendices A–K are reorganized into A–G, regrouping background, derivations, proofs, and experimental details.

P2.justification: The main-text visuals are substantially redesigned: a new communication overview and benchmark figure, a redrawn duality diagram, and a merged three-panel convergence figure replace the earlier arrangement. The outlier figure drops the client-2 column, the NLL convergence panel is omitted, and FashionMNIST blocks move between Tables 1 and 4.

improvement.justification: v3 improves clarity and reproducibility through a clearer Algorithm 1, explicit dual-gradient proofs, better attribution, and a code-access pointer. The redesigned figures and timing comparison also help assess the claims. These gains are tempered by the new sign inconsistency in Appendix B.2 and unexplained MNIST score revisions, supporting a limited overall improvement.
